beliefs.practice: Read the connection string only from an environment variable (e.g., DOCUMENTDB_URI) at runtime; never commit, log, or store the literal URI/credentials in code or repository files.
Use TLS/SSL for all connections and validate server certificates (enable ssl=true / tls=true and disable insecure certificate validation) in the Mongo/Mongoose connection options.

Do not use the cluster admin credentials in the application; create a least-privilege database user (or managed identity/Key Vault-stored credentials) and rotate credentials regularly; read secrets from Key Vault or secure environment variables, not from files.

Choose a partition/shard key that keeps all events for a given paymentReference in the same logical partition (e.g., partition key = paymentReference) to make timeline aggregation single-partition and efficient.

Model each audit event as an immutable document with a unique eventId (UUID) and createdAt timestamp; include paymentReference and a numeric stageSequence to guarantee deterministic ordering independent of clocks.
Enforce immutability and idempotency by (a) using a unique index on eventId and (b) performing inserts as upserts with $setOnInsert or insert-if-not-exists patterns rather than update-based mutation.

Create a compound index that supports the timeline aggregation: { paymentReference: 1, stageSequence: 1, createdAt: 1 } (or paymentReference + createdAt) so $match on paymentReference and $sort by stageSequence/createdAt can be covered and avoid in-memory sorts.

Ensure index creation is executed on the server (createIndexes or Mongoose ensureIndexes) and verify completion with explain() or listIndexes; if a tool (MCP) fails, fall back to createIndexes via the official Mongo API/driver and wait for the index to finish building before relying on it.

For timeline aggregation pipelines, push $match and $project as early as possible, and ensure queries use the index (explain('executionStats') should show an index plan and not a COLLSCAN); enable allowDiskUse:true if pipelines may exceed memory.
Make writes idempotent at the application level: include a client-supplied idempotency/eventId and deduplicate using a unique index or conditional insert so retries do not create duplicate events.

Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and jitter for transient network or throttling errors (check error codes for transient vs permanent), and limit retries; do not retry writes blindly without idempotency keys.

Provision throughput (or choose autoscale) to support expected write bursts from audit events and monitor RU/OPS; set alerts for RU throttling and high latency so you can increase throughput before tail latency impacts ingestion.

Keep small, focused documents for audit events (avoid embedding large binary blobs) and store any large attachments in blob storage with a reference in the event document to reduce document size and indexing cost.
Use Mongoose schema validation (required fields, enums for stage names, types) and set strict mode to reject unexpected fields to prevent malformed or partial audit events being recorded.

Avoid relying solely on application-layer hooks to enforce immutability; where possible restrict DB user privileges so the application account cannot perform update/delete operations, or use database-side controls (roles/privileges) to reduce the blast radius if app code has a bug.

If using vector indexes/features, only create vector indexes on the specific vector field(s) needed and tune index parameters (metric, M/HNSW params, dimensions) to match your vector size and query patterns; do not enable global vector indexing by default.

Use explain('executionStats') on representative queries (timeline aggregation) and check metrics (index usage, docsExamined) to confirm the index is used; if you see COLLSCAN in production increase index coverage or adjust partitioning.
Enable backups and a retention policy appropriate for audit data (or continuous backups/point-in-time restore) so you can recover from accidental deletion or corruption of audit records.

Instrument and emit metrics (ingest rate, write latency, failed inserts, index build time) and logs (do not log secrets) and create alerts for unusual drops in event ingestion rates or spikes in failures.

When using Mongoose with Azure DocumentDB/Mongo API, explicitly set modern driver options (useUnifiedTopology: true, useNewUrlParser: true) and configure connection pooling (maxPoolSize) and timeouts (serverSelectionTimeoutMS) to avoid connection storms on cold start.

If you expect large volumes and need scale-out, design your partition key and indexes for even distribution (avoid low-cardinality keys such as a fixed tenant or stage) and validate distribution with metrics after seeding traffic.

For seed and verification scripts, make them idempotent: create collections and indexes if-not-exists, insert events with unique eventId or upsert with $setOnInsert so repeated runs do not create duplicates.

Use server-side explain and the cluster's management tools (the documentdb MCP or Azure Portal metrics) to validate index builds and query plans; if a provided MCP tool fails to create an index, use the official Mongo driver and then re-run explain to prove improvement.
Consider retention via a TTL index only if business/legal policy allows deletion; otherwise treat audit documents as append-only and provision storage accordingly.
